papers.title: A Robot Should Know When Its Bus Is Gone: A Conservative Dual-Route, Fault-Isolation State Machine for Modular Servo Systems
papers.summary: Low-cost modular robotic arms commonly share serial-bus and power dependencies. A broken connector or local overcurrent can leave an otherwise functional robot unable to complete an authorized task. This technical report presents a minimal, dry-run fault-isolation and alternate-route proposal engine for six simulated servo joints. It represents primary/backup connectivity, measured-current threshold, observation age, explicit owner authorization, and STOP epochs, and generates proposed routes without contacting servos. papers.summary: Accurate 6-DoF object pose estimation and tracking are essential capabilities for robotic systems operating in dynamic environments. papers.summary: Understanding how birds encode object color is fundamental to elucidating the neural mechanisms of color vision. papers.title: Cinematic Space as Textured: Sensorial Horror in Silent Hill (2006)
papers.summary: This essay approaches cinematic space in horror cinema as textured. While texture has often been examined in relation to the felt qualities of the body, especially within the body horror subgenre, I argue that it must also be understood as a property of the spaces that surround and shape embodied experience. Through a close analysis of Silent Hill and its two contrasting textural regimes, I demonstrate that cinematic space functions not simply as a projection of interior psychology but as an active sensory field, whose material qualities organise fear and meaning at the level of perception.
